description: A fine woven fabric such as silk used to face the end leaves for a luxurious finish. It is best paired with a leather joint, glued to paper rather than directly, and damped and ironed before use; its edges fray readily, so they are often turned in over a paper pad.
name: silk end

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter V, p.85. Internet Archive.
